title: Q: Why does Rutherford's nuclear model fail to explain the stability of an atom?
notes: Maxwell's theory states that any accelerating charge radiates electromagnetic energy
An electron orbiting the nucleus is constantly changing direction, so it is constantly accelerating, and by Maxwell's theory it should continuously lose energy as radiation

Losing energy means the electron's orbital radius should shrink, causing it to spiral inward and collapse into the nucleus within a fraction of a second â€” but real atoms are stable, which Rutherford's model cannot account for
